note: P4344 (Pro 29:11) — a fool gives full vent to his spirit; a wise man quietly holds it back.

dims.v: unrestraint — the fool who pours out his whole spirit
the fool who gives full vent to his spirit — pouring out every feeling and impulse without restraint, the opposite of the wise man's quiet self-command
the wise restraint it is set against (266765)
set against the wise who quietly hold it back
kesil (fool) — 'a FOOL gives full vent to his spirit' (cf 12:16; 29:20); folly pours out all it feels, uncontrolled. The fool has no dam against his own impulses.
self-command — the wise who quietly restrains his spirit
the wise man who quietly holds back his spirit — the self-command that governs impulse and keeps its own counsel, the mastery the venting fool lacks
the fool's unrestraint it is set against (266761)
set against the fool who vents everything
chakam (wise) — 'but a wise man quietly HOLDS it back'; wisdom governs the spirit, restraining impulse and keeping calm. Self-command, not venting, is the mark of the wise (cf 16:32; 17:27).
